questions.q: All the gold patches pass. Is the setup cleared?
questions.a: Only the tasks are. A gold patch is applied directly, so it never touches the agent's side: tools, prompts, time limits, memory. To check that side, re-run a model whose ability can't have changed, such as last quarter's, on today's setup.

teach.title: How it works: before you call it a regression

questions.q: How could a stronger model lose points to the setup?
questions.a: Our guess: by doing more. Anthropic's 2026 infrastructure-noise study shows how that can cost points: some models start a Terminal-Bench task by installing a whole data-science stack, and under tight limits the container runs out of memory during that install, before the agent writes a line of solution code.

teach.title: How it works: before you call it a regression

questions.q: Why did moving to execution tests make this more likely?
questions.a: Comparing text with a reference needs no environment. Running tests needs a working one, with the right library versions. Because pip installs the newest version of any unpinned library, an image rebuilt later can contain different code. The SWE-bench-Live team fixed this by only allowing versions released before each task's code.

teach.title: How it works: before you call it a regression

questions.q: What three things does a coding-benchmark score depend on?
questions.a: The model, the harness (tools, prompts, limits) and the environment (the Docker image and its library versions). Only the model's name goes on the score.

questions.q: What does running the gold patches tell you?
questions.a: Whether each task can still be solved in today's container. If the real fix fails, as with the pvlib task under NumPy 2.0.2 in SWE-bench issue #681, the task is broken and its failures say nothing about any model.

teach.title: How it works: before you call it a regression

questions.q: On the same 500 tasks, a new model scores 39% and the old one 38%. Is the new one clearly better?
questions.a: No. At about 39% on 500 tasks, the standard error is about 2.2 points, bigger than the gap. Compare task by task and run more than once before claiming either way.
